answer: Each identity declares a compute budget of 230 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision. Because the karst audit recomputes usage from the ocean history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a inexpensive one. A farm running 32 keys therefore burns for 32 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the wander declaration. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
